issues.description: args[0 + offset] reads as arithmetic noise; collapse to args[offset] or use a single index variable
issues.detail: The expression `args[0 + offset]` is a tell that the author wanted symmetry with `args[2 + offset]` but didn't trust the reader to see it. The data here is small: a list of args plus a starting position. Compute the starting index once (`const start = isRelativeColor ? 2 : 0`) and index `args[start]` and `args[start + 2]`. The algorithm becomes self-evident from the shape of the data and the constant-folding `0 +` disappears.

issues.description: `from` detection is a stringly-typed sniff at args[0]; a tiny helper would make intent obvious
issues.detail: The relative-color test is `args[0]?.value.toLowerCase() === 'from'`. That's fine, but the same check will recur anywhere else this rule (or sibling rules) needs to handle relative color syntax. A one-line helper `isRelativeColor(args)` colocated with the HUE_* constants is the small composable tool. Right now the knowledge that 'from' marks relative color lives inline; later readers have to re-derive it.

issues.description: Filter args once: word-or-function plus skip-from would make findHue a clean transform
issues.detail: `findHue` already filters to word/function nodes. If the relative-color marker `from` is itself a word, you could drop it during the same filter pass (or, more cleanly, slice it off after detection) and then the offset bookkeeping vanishes entirely: HUE_FIRST_ARG_FUNCS picks args[0], HUE_THIRD_ARG_FUNCS picks args[2], regardless of relative-color syntax. That is the Unix-filter shape — strip the prefix, then route by function name on uniform data. Worth considering if this rule grows further.

issues.description: Test fixture for HSL relative color uses non-percentage S/L channels that aren't valid CSS
issues.detail: Several added fixtures (e.g. `hsl(from red 10 s l)`, `hsl(from red 270 60% 50%)` with bare `s`/`l` identifiers) lean on the parser accepting tokens that aren't actually legal CSS-color-5 channel references in every position. Not a correctness bug for this lint rule — the data shape is what's being tested — but worth a comment in the test file explaining these are minimal-parse fixtures, not real-world color values, so a future maintainer doesn't 'fix' them.

review.summary: SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE, mostly. The fix is four lines of carefully-chosen offset arithmetic in the right place — exactly the shape this kind of rule should take. Data dominates: the args array already had the right structure, the patch just teaches the indexing to skip the relative-color prefix. Nits only: collapse `args[0 + offset]` to a single computed start index, consider extracting `isRelativeColor(args)` as a named one-liner so the next rule that needs it can reuse it, and a slice-off-`from` approach would let `findHue` route on uniform data without offset bookkeeping. None of these block merge.
